summary: Rate-shedding policy misfire during tenant surge leading to 5xx retry cascade
description: Issue summary: During an unanticipated tenant traffic surge for NovaChat, the API gateway applied an adaptive rate-shedding policy that mis-evaluated backend capacity, triggering widespread 5xx responses and a client-side retry cascade. Impact: multiple tenant requests returned 502/503 over a 22 minute window; customers reported stream disconnects and elevated latency. Environment: production us-east cluster serving Dedicated pools with mixed prefetch and streaming workloads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate sustained connection burst with many long-lived streaming sessions against tenant NovaChat on prod us-east
2) Force a mixed prompt workload where many requests trigger prefetch and cold KV cache misses
3) Observe API gateway rate-shedding decisions and how upstream runtimes are selected for fallback
4) Watch for client retry behavior and whether retries are amplified by gateway responses (502/503).
logs: 2026-03-13T12:07:12Z apigw[edge-12] WARN shed_decision=adaptive action=drop tenant=novachat sessions=842 backlog=3700
2026-03-13T12:07:13Z runtime[pool-7] ERROR upstream=worker-77 status=exit reason=oom_estimated kernel_swap=false
2026-03-13T12:07:14Z apigw[edge-12] ERROR proxy_response status=502 upstream=worker-77 latency_ms=412
2026-03-13T12:16:02Z apigw[edge-12] INFO shed_decision=adaptive_reenable action=allow tenant=novachat sessions=128 backlog=80
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: adaptive rate-shed policy overreacted to transient backlog signals from the ingress prioritizer and marked a whole tenant as overloaded instead of applying fine-grained shedding. This caused many requests to be rerouted or dropped, prompting heavy client retries and producing a cascading 5xx wave.
Correlated events: a parallel autoscaler jitter event (documented in SUP-214567) reduced warm workers briefly, increasing prefetch latency and inflating backlog signals to the prioritizer.

Telemetry: trace sampling shows increased queue latency on apigw edge nodes between 12:05-12:28 UTC. Heap / memory metrics for several runtime workers show short-lived spikes but not sustained OOMs; a small subset of workers did crash (see logs).
Behavioral note: retry headers from client (Retry-After absent) caused immediate retries; lack of coordinated backoff amplified load on already stressed upsteam workers.

Repro attempt: synthetic load reproduced shed decision when backlog > 1500 and average runtime response time > 250ms. Adjusting shed threshold to 3000 avoided the misfire in test harness but increases risk of degraded latency under real overload.
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Customer reported continuous 502s and streaming disconnects starting 12:04 UTC. Provided initial logs and asked for engineering triage.
Luis Ortega (SRE): Assigned. Spun up diagnostic traces and confirmed apigw shed decisions aligning with backlog spikes. Noted autoscaler chatter from 12:03-12:06 UTC.
Priya Nair (Runtime): Found three worker crashes correlated with prefetch cold path. Opening runtime investigation to check kernel selection and memory accounting.
Avi Patel (Solutions): Escalated to customer success; provided NovaChat with recommended client backoff headers while we investigate.
resolution: Mitigated via staged rollback of aggressive adaptive shed thresholds and temporary enforcement of conservative client backoff recommendations. Engineering deployed a hotfix to scope shed decisions per resource-class instead of tenant-wide, which prevented subsequent 5xx cascades.
resolution_notes: Hotfix deployed 2026-03-13T16:40Z on apigw edge fleet: adaptive_shed.thresholds.tenant_critical increased from 1500 to 3000 and decision granularity changed to resource-class. No further 5xx waves observed after 16:45 UTC.

Runtime team patched memory accounting in the prefetch cold path to avoid transient worker crashes; rollout completed to Dedicated pools by 2026-03-13T18:10Z (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-registry/pull/289).
Customer communications: NovaChat notified of mitigation and recommended to implement exponential backoff with jitter. Support will monitor tenant for 48 hours.
next_steps: 1) Postmortem scheduled: owner Luis Ortega, doc link to be attached to related_confluence_pages. Due 2026-03-20.
2) Add conservative default client backoff guidance to API docs and insert Retry-After header where appropriate within apigw responses.
3) Enhance shed policy tests in chaos harness to include autoscaler jitter scenarios and cold-KV prefetch bursts.
4) Monitor NovaChat dedicated pool for 48 hours and collect SLI deltas; report to CS and product.
